Before stating the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, we record two
prerequisite results.
The usual statement of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
assumes that the integrand $f$ is continuous on $[a, b]$;
continuity is sufficient there, though not necessary.
The two results are
"differentiability implies continuity",
which says where continuity comes from,
and "continuity implies integrability",
which says what continuity buys us.
